SPECIF'KATION FOR INK, FINGER PRINTING, BLACK (

Fr'rstRevision ) 0. FOREWORD

0.1 ThisIndian Standard (First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 31 January &SO, after !he draft finalized by the Inks and Allied Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 This standard was originally published in 1959. The Sectional Committee responsible for its preparation decided to revise it in the light of experience gained since its publication. In this revision, the requirement for consistency and its method of evaluation has been added. 0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value. observed or calculated. expressing the result of a test or analysis. shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960+. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.
1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes requirements and methods of sampling and test for black finger printing ink used for taking impressions of fingers, thumbs and palms for the purpose of identification of persons.

2. REQUIREMENTS 2.1 Description -The material shall consist of a dispersion of carbon black (see IS : 40-1971 t ) with or without admixture of other pigments in a suitable oil base. The colour of the finished material shall be jet black. 2.1.1 The material shall be of uniform consistency, free from grit and other substances likely to act as irritants to human skin. Oils used as vehicle shall preferably be free from odour and in any case shall not have any obnoxious smell. *Rules Ear rounding off numerical values ( revised). +Speci&ation for carbon black (first revision ). 3

Is:1380-1980
2.2 Pigment Content - The material when tested by the method given in 27 of IS : lOI-1964' shall contain'not less than 7-O percent by mass of

pigments. 2.3 Consistency - The consistency of the ink shall be like a soft paste and it shall have iust sufficient tack to enable it to be rolled uniformly on a glass plate with a rubber roller when tested as prescribed in Appendix A. At the same time when the ink is spread on art paper with a rubber roller it shall not pick up any part of the paper surface while spreading on it. 2.4 Applicability - The material when tested by the method prescribed in Appendix B, shall not be inferior to the approved sample. 2.5 Fastness and Smudginess - The prints made by the materia.J when tested by the method prescribed in Appendix C, shall be fast to saline water, dilute acetic acid, organic solvents and ultraviolet light and shaJJ not be affected by rubbing with a finger. 2.6 Relative Density - The relative density of the material at 27�C when tested by the method prescribed in Appendix D shall be 0'980 to O-995.
3. EEEPING

QUALITY

3.1 The material when stored under normal conditions in original sealed containers shall retain the properties detailed in this specification for a minimum period of 2 years from the date of manufacture, 4. APPENDIX
( Clause 2.3 )

A

TEST FOR SUITABILITY OF INK CONSISTENCY A-l. APPARATUS
A-l.1
A-l.2

Glass Plate -A

sheet of glass pIateofsize45x45cmand

15mm

thickness.
Rubber Roller - Made of neoprene rubber sheet, about 2'5 nun in thickness, mounted tightly on a wooden roller. The roller shall be pivoted to a mild steel bracket shaped like a channel about 11 x4x l-2 cm ( outside dimension) and made of 1.5 mm sheet. The roller with the bracket shall be provided with a wooden handle about 12 cm long fitted with brass ferrule 8 mm wide. The roller shall roll freely. A-l.3 Art Paper Sheet - Size, 11 x 11 cm( see IS : 4658-1968. ).

A-2. PROCEDURE A-2.1 Clean the glass plate. Place the 11 x 11 em art paper sheet on the glass plate and take about 1 g of ink on the paper. Spread the ink unif&y on the art paper by rubber roller. After proper spreading of ink, wat& whether the roller is picking up any portion of art paper. If there is no lifting of paper, the ink shall be considered satisfactory.

APPENDIX TF.ST FOR

B

APPLICARILITY

R-l. APPARATUS R-l.1 Glass Plate - Same as in A-1.1. El.2 Rubber Roller - Same as in A-1.2. R-2. PROCEDURE R-2.1 Clean glass plate. Mark on area of 1I x 1 I cm on the plate with a glass marking pencil. Put about 0.5 g of ink within the marked area and spread it uniformly with rubber roller to cover the marked area. B-2.2 When the inked plate is ready, roll the thumb from nail on the plate in one direction and only once at one place. Then roll the thumb on to a glazed card in exactly the same manner as was done on the inked plate. B-2.3 Clean the thumb, and produce another thumb impression using exactly the same procedure with an approved sample of the ink. B-2.4 The impression shall be not inferior with regard to intensity and clean reproduction of the ridge of the thumb than the impression produced by the approved cample of the ink when viewed through a magnifying glass.

APPENDIX ( Clause 2.5 )

C

lTST FOR FASTNESS AND SMUDGINESS
C-l. TEST SPECIMENS C-l.1 Take a few strips ( about 10x 5 cm ) of cream wove/cream laid paper of 60 g/m' ( see IS : 1848-1971*) and make a couple of thumb impressions ( as prescribed in B-2.1 and B-2.2) on each strip. The impression shall be clear and of equal intensity. C-l.2 Smudginess - After 3 minutes of marking the thumb impressions, lightly rub the impressions with a finger. The impressions shall have no tendency to smudge. Cl.3 Fastness to Saline Water - Take a strip with thumb impressions and keep in a solution of sodium chloride ( approximately 10 percent m/v)
*Specification for writing and printing papers (first rev&an).

for one hour at room temperature. The ink shall be consideral fast to saline water if impressions remain clear without any noticeable spreading of ink or loss of intensity. C-l.4 Fastness to Organic Solvents - Take two fresh strips having thumb impressions and keep one in denatured spirit ( see IS : 324-1959 *) and the other in petroleum ether ( see IS .: 1745-1966t ) for one hour. The ink shah be considered fast to organic solvents if the impressions remain clem without any noticeable spreading of ink or loss of intensity. C-l.5 Fastness to Dilute Acetic Acid - Take another strip having thumb impressions and keep for one hour in dilute acetic acid ( 5 percent m/m). at room temperature. The ink shall be considered fast to dilute acetic acid if impressions remain clear without any noticeable spreading of ink or loss of intensity. C-l.6 Ultra-violet Ray Exposure - Place a strip having thumb impressions at a distance of 25 cm from an ultra-violet lamp normal to the rays and expose for 36 hours. The ink shall be considered fast to ultra-vioIet rays if there is no appreciable loss in intensity of thumb impressions. C-1.6.1 The ultra-violet lamp shall be of 125 watts and of long wave UV region, chiefly at 365.5 m/pm.

El.1 Samples shall be drawn from originally unopened tubes.
El.2 Samples shall not be taken in an exposed place.

E-l.3 The sampling apparatus shall be clean and dry whef, used.
~1.4 Precautions shall be taken to protat the samples, I material being sample+, the sampling apparatus and the containers far samples from adventltlous contamination. El.7 Each sample container shall filling, and marked with full details the month and year of manufacture be of such a size that they are almost be sealed airtight with a stopper after of sampling, the date of sampling and of the material.

El.8 Samples shall be stored in such a manner that the temperature of
the material does not vary unduly from the normd temperature.

F-3. TEST SAMPLES AND REFEREE SAMPLE E-3.1 Preparation of Teat Samples F-3.1.1 Squeez out a small portion of the material from each tube selected ( see Table 1 ). Thoroughly mix the material drawn from the same tube. Out of these pOrtiOxJS. I small but equal quantity shall be t&en for C&I stlectad tube and shall be well mixed up together so as to form a ---__ ______ *Methodsfor random sampling. 9

composite sample of quantity sufficient to make triplicate detcrminatkms for all the characteristics to be tested on the composite sample. This composite sample shall be divided into three equal parts, one fn the purchaser, another for the supplier and the third for the referee. E-3.1.2 The remaining portions of the material from each tube ( after a small quantity needed for formation of the composite sample has been taken out ) shall be divided into three equal parts. These parts shall be immediately transferred to thoroughly dried bottles which are then sealed airtight with stoppers and labelled with all the particulars of sampling given under E-1.7. The material in each such sealed bottle shall constitute a test sample. These individual samples shall be separated into three identical sets of test samples in such a way that each set has a test sample representing each tube selected ( see Table 1 ). One of these three sets shall be marked for the purchaser, another for the supplier and the third for the referee. E-3.2 Referee Sample E-3.2.1 Referee sample shall consist of the composite sample ( see E-3.1.1 ) and a set of test samples ( see E-3.1.2 ) marked for the purpose and shall bear the seals of the purchaser and the supplier. This shall be kept at a place agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier and shall be used in case of a dispute between the two. E-4. NUMBER OF TESTS

E-4.1 Tests for applicability and .fastness of the material shall be conducted on each of the samples constituting a set of test samples. E-4.2 Tests for the determination of other characteristics shall be conducted on the composite sample. ES. CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY mentioned in 2

E-5.1 A lot shall be declared as conforming to the specification if it satisfies the requirements for each of the characteristics mentioned in this speci!%ation. E-5.2 If the requirements for any of the characteristics are not met, the lot shall be declared to have not satisfied the requirements of the specification and shall be rejected. .
